title: Walking into Rockhead's in Montreal
summary: He went to Montreal, sat in at Rockhead's Paradise, owned by Jamaican Rufus Rockhead, met Bill Kurzie, and was offered an upstairs band, Rockhead's Rendezvous, with pianist Gertie Waters.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, I went to Montreal to see what was happening for a week or two and there was a place called Rockheads,... Mountain Street, / and they had a band at that time. They always had bands though, and they used American talent. Singles, and all the fellows in the band, they were ex-Americans, most of them, they had children with Canadians.

So, the band, I think the leader of the band was -- I think it was Andy Shorter brothers, they had a pianist his name was Benny and they had the two brothers, alto and tenor, and a boy named Jimmy Jones on the trumpet. Very good trumpet.

So, I luckily, I walked in one Sunday afternoon and played a solo and they wanted to know who I was. I gave him my card and he asked me how long I was staying and I said, well, I can stay here for a week.
So, while the man was doing six nights of business he says, I'm going to make another floor up top, His name was Mr. Rockhead, this man was from Jamaica.
Very polite man. He'd married/and his a French family family -- so, we, I'm happy about this offering.
And I met a fellow, his name was Bill Kurzie. A very quiet person, nice, talk real slow. It would take him two hours to say hello, too.
So, he says, well, Mr. Butler, how would you like to have the band, make a band up, upstairs and we'll call it The Rockheads Rendezvous and I said I'd be delighted/

So, then we had another -- they had a girl and her name was Gertie Waters. She could read all the music, couldn't do some of the jazz, but she would play those chords for you. And Kurzie was a beautiful saxophone player. Beautiful fellow.
